title: ¿Qué opinas?
subtitle: Four ways to ask for and give an opinion
register: casual (tú), a couple at home, Mexican Spanish
review: Notes, translations and questions written by Claude. Check the Spanish, the English lines, the notes and the questions.
intro: A very hot salsa, a shirt with flamingos, a man whose opinions all come from his mother, and a dinner nobody can choose: four short scenes between Emma and Lucas. Listen for ¿qué te parece? and ¿qué opinas?, for yo creo que and para mí, and for the soft ways to say no.

tr.en: Taste my salsa. What do you think?

lines.note: ¿Qué te parece?: what do you think of it? Probar: to taste, to try.
Rico, rica: delicious, said of food. Estar, because it is how it tastes now.
Picar: to be hot, spicy.

lines.text: No, para nada. Yo creo que está perfecta.

tr.en: No, not at all. I think it's perfect.

lines.note: Para nada: not at all. Yo creo que…: I think that…
¿Seguro?: are you sure? To a woman: ¿segura?
Es de la emoción: it's from emotion, I'm so moved.

tr.en: Shall I give you some more?

lines.note: ¿Te sirvo más?: the host's question at the table. Servir: to serve.

lines.text: La verdad… mejor un vaso de agua.

tr.en: Honestly… a glass of water would be better.

lines.note: La verdad…: to tell the truth. Mejor + a thing: I'd rather have that.
Verse bien, verse mal: to look good, to look bad.

lines.text: ¿Bien y ya? ¿Qué opinas de la camisa?

tr.en: Just fine? What do you think of the shirt?

lines.note: ¿Y ya?: and that's all? ¿Qué opinas de…?: what do you think of…?
¿La verdad?: do you want the truth?

tr.en: If you ask me, it's a lot of shirt.

lines.note: Para mí…: for me, in my view. Es mucha camisa: it's too much, too loud.

tr.en: It has flamingos on it, Lucas.

lines.note: Pues: well. A mí me gusta: I like it, whatever you think.

lines.text: Qué bueno. En mi opinión, es perfecta para la fiesta.

tr.en: Good. In my opinion, it's perfect for the party.

lines.note: Qué bueno: that's good. En mi opinión: in my opinion.
¿Verdad que sí?: asks the other person to agree.

lines.text: Sí. Así no te me pierdes.

tr.en: Yes. That way I won't lose you.

lines.note: Así: that way. No te me pierdes: you won't get lost on me. The me says she is the one who would lose him.

lines.text: Mi mamá dice que el sillón va junto a la ventana.

tr.en: My mom says the armchair goes by the window.

lines.note: Dice que…: says that… Junto a: next to. El sillón: an armchair, or a sofa.

tr.en: Uh-huh. And what do you think?

lines.note: ¿Y tú qué opinas?: and what's your opinion? Tú in front means: you, not your mom.

lines.text: Yo pienso que se ve mejor junto a la ventana.

tr.en: I think it looks better by the window.

lines.note: Yo pienso que…: I think that… Se ve mejor: it looks better.
¿Y de…?: and what about…? Short for ¿y qué opinas de…?

lines.text: Mi mamá dice que están muy oscuras.

tr.en: My mom says they're too dark.

lines.note: ¿Qué piensas? = ¿qué opinas?
Tener razón: to be right.

tr.en: Lucas, do you have any opinions of your own?

lines.note: Propio, propia: your own.

lines.text: Deja le pregunto a mi mamá.
lines.note: Deja le pregunto: let me ask her. Spoken Mexican Spanish; in writing, déjame preguntarle.

tr.en: What do you want for dinner?

lines.note: Cenar: to have dinner.
Lo que tú quieras: whatever you like. Quieras is the subjunctive of querer.

tr.en: Hmm, I don't know. I don't think so.

lines.note: No sé: I don't know. No creo: I don't think so, a soft no.
Me da igual: it's all the same to me. Tú decide: you decide.
Pozole: a Mexican soup of hominy corn and meat, made for parties and family weekends.
En martes: on a Tuesday, an ordinary weekday.

lines.text: Tengo la impresión de que no te da igual.

tr.en: I get the feeling you do mind.

lines.note: Tengo la impresión de que…: I get the feeling that…

notes: Asking: ¿qué te parece?, ¿qué opinas de…?, ¿y tú qué opinas?, ¿y tú qué piensas?, ¿cómo me veo?
Giving an opinion: yo creo que…, yo pienso que…, para mí…, en mi opinión…, tengo la impresión de que…
Liking: a mí me gusta, está muy rica (food), se ve mejor (it looks better).
A soft no: no sé, no creo. A firm one: no, para nada.
Not choosing: lo que tú quieras, me da igual, tú decide.
Before the truth: ¿la verdad?, la verdad…
Mexican spoken Spanish: ¿cómo me veo?, deja le pregunto, ajá, qué bueno.

questions.q: Emma wants Lucas's opinion of her salsa. What does she ask?
questions.why: ¿Qué te parece? asks for an opinion. ¿Cómo me veo? asks how you look.

questions.q: Why is Lucas red and crying?
questions.why: He blames the heat and his feelings, but in the end he asks for a glass of water.

questions.q: Why does Emma think the shirt is perfect for the party?
questions.why: Así no te me pierdes: with flamingos on, he is easy to find.

questions.q: Who decides where the armchair goes?
questions.why: Mi mamá dice que el sillón va junto a la ventana. Lucas only agrees.
Me da igual: it's all the same to me. Emma says it, but she does not mean it.
